mechanism_narrative: A lower current federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) compresses discount rates for equity valuation, producing positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days. The relationship is negative: lower FEDFUNDS directly predicts higher returns.
failure_condition: FEDFUNDS level shows no significant positive correlation with 20-day S&P 500 returns (Rank IC < 0.03 over any 3-year rolling window) or the relationship reverses in more than 40% of market regimes.

mechanism_narrative: When the unemployment rate (UNRATE) exceeds 6.5%, it signals deteriorating labor market conditions increasing recession risk, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: UNRATE > 6.5% occurs in 60% of cases but S&P 500 produces positive 20-day returns in more than 40% of those instances (p-value > 0.05 for negative return expectation).

mechanism_narrative: The joint condition of low federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS < 0.5%) and high unemployment (UNRATE > 6.0%) indicates recessionary monetary policy response, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: The joint condition (FEDFUNDS < 0.5% AND UNRATE > 6.0%) occurs in 30% of market observations but S&P 500 returns are positive in more than 50% of these cases (p-value > 0.05 for negative return expectation).

mechanism_narrative: In a monetary tightening cycle (FEDFUNDS > 2.0% over past 3 months), reduced liquidity and increased risk aversion cause negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: The FEDFUNDS > 2.0% condition occurs in 25% of market observations but S&P 500 returns are positive in more than 40% of these cases (p-value > 0.05 for negative return expectation).

mechanism_narrative: A higher current level of housing starts (HOUST) indicates strong consumer demand and economic expansion, producing positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days. The relationship is positive: higher HOUST directly predicts higher returns.
failure_condition: HOUST level shows no significant positive correlation with 5-day S&P 500 returns (Rank IC < 0.03 over any 3-year rolling window) or the relationship reverses in more than 40% of market regimes.

mechanism_narrative: When industrial production (INDPRO) falls below 95.0, it signals manufacturing sector contraction increasing recession risk, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: INDPRO < 95.0 occurs in 20% of market observations but S&P 500 returns are positive in more than 50% of these cases (p-value > 0.05 for negative return expectation).

mechanism_narrative: The joint condition of strong housing starts (HOUST > 900) and moderate inflation (CPIAUCSL > 2.5% annualized) indicates healthy economic expansion, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: The joint condition (HOUST > 900 AND CPIAUCSL > 2.5%) occurs in 30% of market observations but S&P 500 returns are negative in more than 50% of these cases (p-value > 0.05 for positive return expectation).

mechanism_narrative: In a labor market tightening cycle (PAYEMS growth rate > 0.5% quarterly), anticipated wage-driven inflation and subsequent monetary tightening cause negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: The PAYEMS growth rate > 0.5% condition occurs in 25% of market observations but S&P 500 returns are positive in more than 40% of these cases (p-value > 0.05 for negative return expectation).
